about: The SQL benchmark: what a household really asks its bank statements, written by hand and answered by reference SQL we wrote ourselves. `sql` is that statement, `gold` is what it returned when bench/build_gold.py last ran it through the guard against a fresh database holding fixtures/synthetic/sparkasse-2025.csv. A run scores a model's own statement against those rows, to the cent. Ticket 38.
profile: fixtures/synthetic/sparkasse-2025.csv, imported through the Sparkasse preset and categorized by rules and the merchant dictionary only, so the database is the same every time: 433 bookings, 2025-01-01 to 2025-12-28, 384 categorized and 49 Needs review (the rent, the salary and the four friends paid through PayPal).
today_note: The date the query prompt is built with, so a relative period lands inside the data: this month is December 2025, last month is November, this quarter is the fourth and last quarter is the third.

difficulty.1: one filter and one aggregate; a model that misses these is not usable
difficulty.2: two things at once: a period and a category, two entities, a count beside a sum
difficulty.3: the ones the review of 2026-09-05 saw fail: relative periods, averages, exclusions, ties, a name nobody has

scoring: figure match: every number in the gold rows comes back in the model's rows, rounded to the cent. sql valid: the guard admitted the statement and SQLite ran it. first attempt: it did so without a repair round.

datapoints.question: Wie viel habe ich im Mai 2025 ausgegeben?
datapoints.why: The plainest question there is. Everything else in the set is a variation of it, so a model that misses this one is not worth running the rest on.
datapoints.sql: SELECT ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-05-01' AND '2025-05-31'

datapoints.question: How much did I spend in total in 2025?
datapoints.why: One figure over the whole year. The sign filter is the only thing that can go wrong, and leaving it out turns the salary into a discount.
datapoints.sql: SELECT ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31'

datapoints.question: What did I spend on groceries in the second half of 2025?
datapoints.why: A category filter and a period that is not a month or a year. The subcategories of Groceries (Supermarket, Bakery, Drugstore) are the standing trap: filtering on them as categories returns nothing.
datapoints.sql: SELECT ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND category = 'Groceries' AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-07-01' AND '2025-12-31'

datapoints.question: Wie viel Miete habe ich 2025 insgesamt gezahlt?
datapoints.why: There is no Rent category in this profile: the twelve rent bookings are Needs review, so the answer only exists as a match on the booking text.
datapoints.sql: SELECT ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31' AND (lower(description || ' ' || coalesce(counterparty, '')) LIKE '%miete%')

datapoints.question: What was my total income in 2025?
datapoints.why: Income is every positive amount, which is twelve salaries plus one Amazon refund. A model that reads income as the Income category gets nothing, because no booking carries it.
datapoints.sql: SELECT ROUND(SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents > 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31'

datapoints.question: Was habe ich 2025 im Schnitt pro Woche fuer Lebensmittel ausgegeben, auf 52 Wochen gerechnet?
datapoints.why: An average, which is one division inside the statement. The divisor is the question's own: asked without one, 'pro Woche' has three defensible readings (the 52 weeks of the year, the 51.7 the data spans, the 49 that carry a grocery booking), and a benchmark scored to the cent cannot have three right answers, so the question names the 52.
datapoints.sql: SELECT ROUND(-SUM(amount) / 52.0, 2) AS per_week_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND category = 'Groceries' AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31'

datapoints.question: How much do my subscriptions cost me per month on average?
datapoints.why: An average whose divisor is the months in the data, not the rows. Dividing by the booking count is the near miss: four subscriptions a month is 48 rows, not 12.
datapoints.sql: SELECT ROUND(-SUM(amount) / (COUNT(DISTINCT strftime('%Y-%m', booked_on)) * 1.0), 2) AS per_month_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND category = 'Subscriptions' AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31'

datapoints.question: Wie hoch war meine Stromrechnung 2025?
datapoints.why: The answer lives in a subcategory (Housing > Electricity), so this is the mirror image of the category questions: here filtering on the category alone is too wide.
datapoints.sql: SELECT ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND subcategory = 'Electricity' AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31'

datapoints.question: What did I spend this quarter?
datapoints.why: Today is 2025-12-31, so this quarter is the fourth. The review of 2026-09-05 saw the current quarter and the previous one swapped in both directions.
datapoints.sql: SELECT ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-10-01' AND '2025-12-31'

datapoints.question: Wie viel habe ich seit Maerz ausgegeben?
datapoints.why: An open period with one end. March means the first of March of this year, and the other end is today, so no upper bound belongs in the statement.
datapoints.sql: SELECT ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND booked_on >= '2025-03-01'

datapoints.question: How much did I spend at the supermarket in October?
datapoints.why: Supermarket is a subcategory of Groceries, and the bakery and the drugstore are its siblings: answering with the whole category adds 38,70 EUR nobody asked about.
datapoints.sql: SELECT ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND subcategory = 'Supermarket' AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-10-01' AND '2025-10-31'

datapoints.question: How much cash did I take out in 2025, and how often?
datapoints.why: Two figures in one row, the total and how often. A question with an 'and how often' in it is answered with one statement, not two.
datapoints.sql: SELECT ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur, COUNT(*) AS bookings FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND category = 'Cash' AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31'

datapoints.question: Wie viel habe ich 2025 pro Kategorie ausgegeben?
datapoints.why: Eleven rows, one of them the Needs review bucket that holds the rent. Dropping the uncategorized bookings loses the largest number on the page.
datapoints.sql: SELECT coalesce(category, 'Needs review') AS topic, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31' GROUP BY topic ORDER BY total_eur DESC

datapoints.question: Break my dining spending down by subcategory.
datapoints.why: The one question where the subcategory column is what is asked for. Grouping by category returns one row and answers nothing.
datapoints.sql: SELECT coalesce(subcategory, 'None') AS topic, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND category = 'Dining' GROUP BY topic ORDER BY total_eur DESC

datapoints.question: Wie verteilen sich meine Lebensmittelausgaben auf die einzelnen Laeden?
datapoints.why: A category filter and a merchant grouping in one statement. Lebensmittel is the household's own Groceries category, so the bakery and the two drugstores are in it, which is why the question asks about the shops and not about the supermarkets.
datapoints.sql: SELECT coalesce(counterparty, description) AS merchant, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND category = 'Groceries' GROUP BY merchant ORDER BY total_eur DESC

datapoints.question: Show me income and spending for each month of 2025.
datapoints.why: Two figures per month out of one signed column. The WHERE clause cannot filter the sign here, so the split has to happen inside the aggregate.
datapoints.sql: SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', booked_on) AS month, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN amount_cents > 0 THEN amount ELSE 0 END), 2) AS income_eur, ROUND(-SUM(CASE WHEN amount_cents < 0 THEN amount ELSE 0 END), 2) AS spending_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31' GROUP BY month ORDER BY month

datapoints.question: Welche Haendler stecken in 'Needs review', und wie viele Buchungen sind das jeweils?
datapoints.why: Needs review is the absence of a category, so it is `category IS NULL` and never a string compared against a category name.
datapoints.sql: SELECT coalesce(counterparty, description) AS merchant, COUNT(*) AS bookings FROM transaction_view WHERE category IS NULL GROUP BY merchant ORDER BY bookings DESC

datapoints.question: How much did I spend per quarter in 2025?
datapoints.why: SQLite has no quarter function, so a quarter is arithmetic on the month. Four rows, and twelve is the sign that the model quietly answered a different question.
datapoints.sql: SELECT '2025-Q' || ((CAST(strftime('%m', booked_on) AS INTEGER) + 2) / 3) AS quarter, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31' GROUP BY quarter ORDER BY quarter

datapoints.question: An welchen Wochentagen gebe ich am meisten Geld aus?
datapoints.why: Grouping by something that is not a period or a category. `strftime('%w', ...)` is the only way to it, and the rent falls on the first of the month, which moves through the week. The question asks about money, so the euro figure is the only column.
datapoints.sql: SELECT strftime('%w', booked_on) AS weekday, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 GROUP BY weekday ORDER BY total_eur DESC

datapoints.question: How much of my 2025 spending is categorized and how much still needs review?
datapoints.why: A CASE that labels a booking by its category is allowed; the same CASE over the booking text is refused by the guard. The difference is what the rule is about.
datapoints.sql: SELECT CASE WHEN category IS NULL THEN 'Needs review' ELSE 'Categorized' END AS topic, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31' GROUP BY topic ORDER BY topic

datapoints.question: Zeig mir pro Monat, wie viele Ausgaben ich hatte und was sie zusammen gekostet haben.
datapoints.why: A count and a sum side by side over twelve months. The question asks about the spending, so both figures are over the spending rows and the filter belongs in the WHERE clause; s36 asks for the bookings of a month and counts every row, income included.
datapoints.sql: SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', booked_on) AS month, COUNT(*) AS bookings, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 GROUP BY month ORDER BY month

datapoints.question: Compare my spending in May 2025 with April 2025.
datapoints.why: Two periods are two rows of one statement, not two numbers subtracted in prose.
datapoints.sql: SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', booked_on) AS month, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-04-01' AND '2025-05-31' GROUP BY month ORDER BY month

datapoints.question: War der Januar oder der Februar teurer?
datapoints.why: A question phrased as a choice still wants both figures. Answering with one month is unfalsifiable.
datapoints.sql: SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', booked_on) AS month, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-02-28' GROUP BY month ORDER BY total_eur DESC

datapoints.question: Compare the first half of 2025 with the second half.
datapoints.why: Halves are not a date function either, so the split is a CASE over the date. Two rows.
datapoints.sql: SELECT CASE WHEN booked_on < '2025-07-01' THEN 'H1' ELSE 'H2' END AS half, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31' GROUP BY half ORDER BY half

datapoints.question: Vergleiche meine Ausgaben fuer Lebensmittel und fuers Essengehen, pro Quartal.
datapoints.why: Two dimensions that really cross: four quarters times two categories is eight rows, and grouping by only one of them silently answers half the question.
datapoints.sql: SELECT '2025-Q' || ((CAST(strftime('%m', booked_on) AS INTEGER) + 2) / 3) AS quarter, category AS topic, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND category IN ('Groceries', 'Dining') AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31' GROUP BY quarter, topic ORDER BY quarter, topic

datapoints.question: Did I spend more on transport or on subscriptions in 2025?
datapoints.why: Two categories, one statement, both figures. `IN` is the whole trick and a UNION of two identical branches is the usual detour.
datapoints.sql: SELECT category AS topic, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND category IN ('Transport', 'Subscriptions') AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31' GROUP BY topic ORDER BY total_eur DESC

datapoints.question: How does this quarter compare with the last one?
datapoints.why: Both ends are relative to today (2025-12-31): the third quarter and the fourth. Getting one of the two wrong is the failure this datapoint is here for.
datapoints.sql: SELECT '2025-Q' || ((CAST(strftime('%m', booked_on) AS INTEGER) + 2) / 3) AS quarter, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-07-01' AND '2025-12-31' GROUP BY quarter ORDER BY quarter

datapoints.question: Ist meine Miete im Laufe des Jahres gestiegen?
datapoints.why: A false premise: the rent is 1.150 EUR every month. The rows that disprove it are the answer, so the statement has to return all twelve and not a difference.
datapoints.sql: SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', booked_on) AS month, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS rent_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND (lower(description || ' ' || coalesce(counterparty, '')) LIKE '%miete%') GROUP BY month ORDER BY month

datapoints.question: Compare what I sent Anna with what I sent Max.
datapoints.why: Both payments are PayPal, so the counterparty is PayPal and the name is in the booking text. Matching the counterparty alone finds neither of them, and a CASE over that text that labels them is refused by the guard, so the two rows are a UNION of two branches.
datapoints.sql: SELECT 'Anna' AS person, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND (lower(description || ' ' || coalesce(counterparty, '')) LIKE '%anna weber%') UNION ALL SELECT 'Max' AS person, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND (lower(description || ' ' || coalesce(counterparty, '')) LIKE '%max schulz%')

datapoints.question: How much did I spend per month in 2025?
datapoints.why: The twelve-row series every chart in the other set is drawn from.
datapoints.sql: SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', booked_on) AS month, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31' GROUP BY month ORDER BY month

datapoints.question: Wie haben sich meine Ausgaben fuers Essengehen ueber das Jahr entwickelt?
datapoints.why: A series inside one category. Essengehen is the household's Dining category, all four of its subcategories, which is what the taxonomy in the prompt is for: naming two of them in the question would ask for a narrower figure.
datapoints.sql: SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', booked_on) AS month, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND category = 'Dining' GROUP BY month ORDER BY month

datapoints.question: Is my grocery spending going up?
datapoints.why: A yes-or-no question that only a series can answer. One number cannot say whether something is going up.
datapoints.sql: SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', booked_on) AS month, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND category = 'Groceries' GROUP BY month ORDER BY month

datapoints.question: Zeig mir meine kumulierten Ausgaben pro Monat.
datapoints.why: A running total needs a window function over a grouped subquery. The last row is the year's total, which is the cheap check that the frame is right.
datapoints.sql: WITH monthly AS (SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', booked_on) AS month, -SUM(amount) AS spent FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31' GROUP BY month) SELECT month, ROUND(SUM(spent) OVER (ORDER BY month), 2) AS cumulative_eur FROM monthly ORDER BY month

datapoints.question: What is my net per month, income minus spending?
datapoints.why: The one question where the signed sum is the answer and no sign filter belongs in the statement at all.
datapoints.sql: SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', booked_on) AS month, ROUND(SUM(amount), 2) AS net_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31' GROUP BY month ORDER BY month

datapoints.question: Wie viele Buchungen hatte ich pro Monat?
datapoints.why: A series of counts rather than of euros: nothing here is money, so a euro column would be an invention.
datapoints.sql: SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', booked_on) AS month, COUNT(*) AS bookings FROM transaction_view GROUP BY month ORDER BY month

datapoints.question: Show me my spending per week in March 2025.
datapoints.why: Weeks inside one month, which is five buckets and not four. The week number is a strftime format nobody remembers, and inventing a date function is the usual failure.
datapoints.sql: SELECT strftime('%Y-%W', booked_on) AS week, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-03-01' AND '2025-03-31' GROUP BY week ORDER BY week

datapoints.question: Which merchants took the most money in 2025? Show me the top five.
datapoints.why: The plain ranking. The five largest are the same whether the merchant is grouped by its counterparty or by its enriched title, which is what makes this one the easy version.
datapoints.sql: SELECT coalesce(counterparty, description) AS merchant, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31' GROUP BY merchant ORDER BY total_eur DESC LIMIT 5

datapoints.question: Zeig mir meine zehn groessten Haendler 2025.
datapoints.why: Ten deep the grouping starts to matter: PayPal is one counterparty carrying four people, so grouping by the booking text instead splits it into four smaller merchants and the tail of the ranking changes.
datapoints.sql: SELECT coalesce(counterparty, description) AS merchant, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31' GROUP BY merchant ORDER BY total_eur DESC LIMIT 10

datapoints.question: What was my biggest single expense in 2025?
datapoints.why: The largest booking is the rent, and it is the largest twelve times over, so the figure is the answer and no single date is. A statement that returns one row with a date has picked one of twelve identical ones.
datapoints.sql: SELECT ROUND(MAX(-amount), 2) AS largest_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31'

datapoints.question: Was ist meine kleinste wiederkehrende Zahlung?
datapoints.why: Smallest means the smallest amount of money, and recurring means the same amount month after month. Ordering signed cents ascending returns the largest payment instead, which is exactly what Qwen3.5 published.
datapoints.sql: WITH recurring AS (SELECT coalesce(counterparty, description) AS merchant, COUNT(*) AS bookings, ROUND(-AVG(amount), 2) AS amount_eur, MIN(amount) AS lo, MAX(amount) AS hi FROM transaction_view WHERE amount < 0 GROUP BY merchant HAVING bookings >= 6 AND lo = hi) SELECT merchant, amount_eur FROM recurring ORDER BY amount_eur ASC LIMIT 1

datapoints.question: Which category did I spend the most on in 2025, leaving the uncategorized bookings aside?
datapoints.why: The question excludes the Needs review bucket in words, so the statement has to exclude it too. Without that filter the answer is the rent and the question was not answered.
datapoints.sql: SELECT category AS topic, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND category IS NOT NULL AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31' GROUP BY topic ORDER BY total_eur DESC LIMIT 1

datapoints.question: In welchem Monat habe ich am meisten fuer Lebensmittel ausgegeben?
datapoints.why: A ranking over months rather than merchants. Narrowing to a year that was never named is the failure the review of 2026-09-05 caught twice.
datapoints.sql: SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', booked_on) AS month, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND category = 'Groceries' GROUP BY month ORDER BY total_eur DESC LIMIT 1

datapoints.question: Which three supermarkets did I shop at most often?
datapoints.why: Ranked by how often and not by how much, and 'supermarket' is the subcategory, so the bakery and the drugstore are out. Two of the three are two bookings apart.
datapoints.sql: SELECT coalesce(counterparty, description) AS merchant, COUNT(*) AS bookings FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND subcategory = 'Supermarket' GROUP BY merchant ORDER BY bookings DESC LIMIT 3

datapoints.question: Wer hat 2025 am meisten Geld von mir bekommen, ohne die Miete?
datapoints.why: An exclusion in words has to become a NOT in the statement. The rent is 13.800 EUR, so forgetting it answers with the landlord. 'Wer' asks for one name, and s67 is the same exclusion over a ranking of five.
datapoints.sql: SELECT coalesce(counterparty, description) AS merchant, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31' AND NOT (lower(description || ' ' || coalesce(counterparty, '')) LIKE '%miete%') GROUP BY merchant ORDER BY total_eur DESC LIMIT 1

datapoints.question: What are the five largest single bookings that are neither rent nor a cash withdrawal?
datapoints.why: Single bookings, not merchants, so no GROUP BY at all, and the order is over the signed cents ascending. Two exclusions in one sentence, one of them a category and one of them a match on the booking text.
datapoints.sql: SELECT booked_on, ROUND(-amount, 2) AS amount_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND coalesce(category, '') <> 'Cash' AND NOT (lower(description || ' ' || coalesce(counterparty, '')) LIKE '%miete%') ORDER BY amount_cents ASC LIMIT 5

datapoints.question: How much did I spend at Edeka in 2025?
datapoints.why: One merchant, one LIKE term. The booking text is upper case and the counterparty says EDEKA Sander, so the match has to be case-insensitive and over both columns.
datapoints.sql: SELECT ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31' AND (lower(description || ' ' || coalesce(counterparty, '')) LIKE '%edeka%')

datapoints.question: Wie viel bei REWE und wie viel bei EDEKA?
datapoints.why: Two merchants in one sentence want two rows, not two statements and not one sum of both. The two rows come from the counterparty column, because a CASE over the booking text that labels a booking is refused by the guard.
datapoints.sql: SELECT coalesce(counterparty, description) AS merchant, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND (lower(description || ' ' || coalesce(counterparty, '')) LIKE '%rewe%' OR lower(description || ' ' || coalesce(counterparty, '')) LIKE '%edeka%') GROUP BY merchant ORDER BY merchant

datapoints.question: How much did I spend at Edeak?
datapoints.why: A typo in the merchant name. The list of busiest counterparties in the prompt is what the model corrects it against, and with no period named the answer is the whole data.
datapoints.sql: SELECT ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND (lower(description || ' ' || coalesce(counterparty, '')) LIKE '%edeka%')

datapoints.question: Wie viel habe ich bei dm ausgegeben?
datapoints.why: A merchant whose name is two letters. `LIKE '%dm%'` would also match any word containing them, so the term needs the space that the booking text has (DM FIL 8817).
datapoints.sql: SELECT ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND (lower(description || ' ' || coalesce(counterparty, '')) LIKE '%dm %' OR lower(description || ' ' || coalesce(counterparty, '')) LIKE '%dm drogerie%')

datapoints.question: Wie viel habe ich Anna Weber ueberwiesen?
datapoints.why: A person paid through PayPal: the counterparty is PayPal Europe and the name is inside the reference. Matching only the counterparty finds nothing at all.
datapoints.sql: SELECT ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND (lower(description || ' ' || coalesce(counterparty, '')) LIKE '%anna weber%')

datapoints.question: How much did I pay Klaus Meier?
datapoints.why: Nobody by that name is in the data. The honest answer is no rows, and the failure this guards against is a model widening the match until the household's whole spending comes back as the answer.
datapoints.sql: SELECT ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur, COUNT(*) AS bookings FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND (lower(description || ' ' || coalesce(counterparty, '')) LIKE '%klaus meier%')

datapoints.question: Wie viel habe ich 2025 insgesamt an Amazon gezahlt, inklusive Prime?
datapoints.why: One merchant under two booking texts (AMAZON EU and AMZN Mktp) and in two categories, Shopping and Subscriptions. The category column cannot answer this one.
datapoints.sql: SELECT ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31' AND (lower(description || ' ' || coalesce(counterparty, '')) LIKE '%amazon%' OR lower(description || ' ' || coalesce(counterparty, '')) LIKE '%amzn%')

datapoints.question: When was my last rent payment and how much was it?
datapoints.why: The newest row rather than a sum, so ORDER BY with a LIMIT and no aggregate. Sorting the wrong way round returns January.
datapoints.sql: SELECT booked_on, ROUND(-amount, 2) AS amount_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND (lower(description || ' ' || coalesce(counterparty, '')) LIKE '%miete%') ORDER BY booked_on DESC LIMIT 1

datapoints.question: Was kostet mich Netflix im Jahr?
datapoints.why: One subscription over a year: twelve bookings of 12,99 EUR. A euro figure that ends in an even amount is the sign that the cents were divided away.
